lawyer: Tawfique Newas with Md. Shorful Islam Khan, Advocate ----- For the Appellant-Petitioner
parties:
Victory Wall Development Ltd ------ Appellant-Petitioner
vs.
Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. and another ------ Proforma Respondent
full_judgment:
Mohammad Asaduzzaman J: This Rule arises out of an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 14/17 days in filing an appeal under section 285 of the Companies Act, 1994. 

 In Company Matter No. 14 of 1994, which is an application under section 166 read with section 162 of the Companies Act, 1913 filed by the petitioner on 26.2.94 for winding up of the respondent Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd. a notice by the Company Judge, High Court Division was issued on 6.3.94 asking the respondent bank to show cause why the application for its winding up should not be admitted. Thereafter an affidavit-of-compliance of service of notice was filed by the petitioner on 31.3.1994. On receipt of the notice of show cause the respondent bank filed a counter affidavit on 2.5.94. Then on 8.5.94 an application was made by the respondent bank to provide security for costs as the petitioner was a foreign Company with no assets in Bangladesh. The petitioner filed an affidavit-in-opposition to the application of the respondent asking for security for costs on 10.5.84. The learned Company Bench on hearing both sides directed the petitioner to furnish security and in compliance of the direction petitioner filed an indemnity bond on 13.6.1994. The petitioner company then filed an affidavit-in-reply to the affidavit-in-opposition. After exchange of these affidavits, the petitioner moved an application challenging the locus standi of the respondent Islami Bank before admission of the winding up application, contending, inter alia, that the show cause notice served upon the respondent bank prior to compliance of the Rules 52-57 of the Supreme Court Rules framed by the full Court, was without jurisdiction and that the same was not in accordance with the rules as adopted by this hon'ble court. The learned Company Judge, High Court Division on hearing the parties by his judgment and order dated 1.9.94 was pleased to reject the said application of the petitioner. The petitioner thereafter, on 20.2.1995 preferred an appeal being Company Appeal No. 3 of 1995 against the aforesaid judgment and order dated 1.9.94 passed by the Company Judge of the High Court Division and the Stamp Reporter initially reported that the appeal has been filed with a delay of 34 days. Whereupon an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act 1908 praying for condonation of delay of only 14 days was filed by the petitioner and by the same application the petitioner submitted that the stamp reporter was absolutely wrong in giving a report of delay of 34 days In view of above submission of the petition, the office was directed to give a fresh report to the effect of actual delay caused in filing the appeal and in compliance of the above order of this court, the Stamp Reporter after carefully calculating the period of delay stated that there has been a delay of 17 days only in filing the appeal. The learned counsel for the petitioner thereafter, submitted a supplementary affidavit explaining the entire period of the delay. In any case, on hearing the learned Advocate of the petitioner, a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause why the delay of 17 days as per subsequent report in filing the appeal should not be condoned. The said Rule now having been made ready is taken up today for hearing. 

 3. The learned Counsel for the petitioner at the very outset submits that he is very much conscious and aware of the established principle that in an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the petitioner is required to explain the delay of each and every day chronologically. 

 4. The learned Counsel then submits that the judgment and order in the application for non- compliance with Rules 52-57 inclusive in Company Matter No. 14 of 1994 was delivered in open Court in the afternoon of Thursday of 1.9.1994 and thereafter an application was made by the petitioner appellant for certified copy of the said judgment and order on the next working day, i.e. Saturday 3.9.1994. The learned Counsel for the petitioner further submits that notification in Register in respect of the estimate, appeared 98 days after the judgment and order on 1.9.1994, during which for the entire period, the petitioner appellant kept close watch as to when such notification would appear. He also submits that the petitioner appellant filed necessary stamp and folios on 13.12.1994 after said above notification on 8.12.1994 that is 4 days after notification and thereby lost 4 days in the calculation of time for purpose of limitation. The petitioner regrets for those 4 days of delay having been caused due to inadvertence. The learned Counsel for the petitioner also submits that the certified copy of the judgment and order became available on 21.1.95 and on receipt of that certified copy the petitioner appellant filed the present Company Appeal No. 3 of 1995 on 20.2.1995 i.e. on the 30th day after receiving the certified copy of the said judgment and order on the mistaken assumption that the appeal would have to be filed within 30 days of availability of the certified copy of the impugned judgment. 

 5. In support of his contention of bonafide mistake of law the learned Counsel cited a decision reported in (1) 25 DLR 203, wherein it has been decided that ignorance of law accompanied by circumstances not indicating want of good faith or diligence may furnish as sufficient ground for condonation of delay. (2) In the decision reported in 29 DLR 259, it has been decided that mistaken advice given by a legal practitioner may in the circumstances of a particular case give rise to sufficient cause within section 5 of the Limitation Act though there is certainly no general doctrine which saves parties from the result of wrong advice. 

 6. The learned Counsel submitted that the petitioner appellant's mistaken belief was caused through his Advocate or Clerk to the effect of limitation of 30 days instead of 20 days and because of this genuine mistake of law the petitioner was delayed by 10 days. Thus is the petitioner's above explanation of delay of 14 days (4 days + 10 days due to mistake of law) and the petitioner still maintains that the Stamp Reporter has gone wrong in his latest report of delay of 17 days. The rest 3 days of delay also appears to have been sufficiently explained. 

 7. Heard the learned Counsel, perused the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, including the supplementary affidavit of the petitioner. Considering the above and the verbal submissions made by the learned Counsel we are satisfied that the petitioner has been able to explain the delay and to show sufficient cause in filing the appeal. Hence we are inclined to accept the explanation as given and find substance in the Rule. 

 8. In the result the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act is allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is condoned. The Rule is accordingly made absolute.
